findings.claim: [Spring 20] The 70% pass mark works as all-or-nothing in practice. Every check first places one normal order (the gate is needed so the checks cannot pass by doing nothing), so the matrix only shows 0, 2, 4 or 6 out of 6. No tested variant scores 5/6; only the self-admitted bulk-update false-fail would land there. Pass therefore means 6/6. One slip in the 2-statement addLine helper (N7 one-sided addLine, N6 lines not saved) scores 0/6, even when the @Transactional work (the main objective) is right. There is no partial credit for the helper objective (one-to-many#o3) apart from the transaction objective.
findings.recommendation: Add 1-2 ungated checks, for example a plain-Java check that calls PickupOrder.addLine and asserts both sides are set. Re-run the matrix, then either confirm that a realistic single flaw now passes at 70%, or declare this item mastery-graded (pass = all checks) in blueprint and README so the programme aggregate accounts for it. Pilot with learners before release.

location.selector: originally spring-short-coding/spring-20min/README.md line 80 (not part of this item's landed files)

findings.claim: [Spring 20] Time-box is tight, and a timing overrun becomes a fail. The authors' median estimate is 15 of 20 minutes. Reading is about 1,000 words (README plus 6 Java files) and there are about 4 test runs at 50-76 s each on the authoring host. A learner who only finds the transaction requirement when the outage checks fail needs more test cycles. Combined with the all-or-nothing scoring above, any overrun is a fail.
findings.recommendation: Pilot with 3-5 learners. Meanwhile, shorten 'What is provided' (drop rows the task text already repeats) and tell learners to read OrderService, PickupOrder and Product only.

findings.claim: [Spring 20] Plain language: 'SKU' is never defined, and 'click-and-collect' and 'owning side' are jargon in a timed setting. Task 3 ('as an outage would: then too, nothing may change') reads awkwardly for non-native readers.
findings.recommendation: Write 'SKU (product code)' the first time it appears. Rewrite task 3 as: 'The checks also make the database reject one write (the order, a line or a stock change). Your code must still leave everything unchanged.'

findings.claim: [Spring 10] The item can be passed without showing its first claimed objective (global-error-handling#o1, one @RestControllerAdvice). N6 builds the 404 in the controller with no advice and passes at 4/5. The authors admit a controller-local @ExceptionHandler would score 5/5 (line 99, not run as a variant). A learner can pass the final on this item without ever using a global handler.
findings.recommendation: Add an assertion that a second controller's ToolNotFoundException is also handled. For example, ship a tiny provided controller (e.g. GET /api/tools/{id}/label) that calls the same service; only an advice covers both. Alternatively, drop the global-error-handling#o1 claim and keep only ProblemDetail#o1.

findings.claim: [Spring 10] The run-time expectation is understated. The README says one run takes 'about half a minute or more', but the measured runs were 68-84 s (loaded host). On a 10-minute item, 3 runs can use 3-4 minutes, which squeezes the authors' 7-minute median.
findings.recommendation: Say 'about a minute' and suggest finishing all three edits before the first run. Measure on an idle reference laptop, or in the Exa template, before release.

findings.claim: [Spring 10] Check 5 (no trace, no 'Exception' text) measures global-error-handling#o3 (never expose internals), but the item claims only o1 and ProblemDetail#o1, so the alignment record understates what is measured.
findings.recommendation: Add global-error-handling#o3 (partial) to the objectives, or note in lab.json that check 5 is supporting evidence, not a claimed objective.

findings.claim: [Spring 10] Spring 10 is close to a composite of four module-lab tasks: spring-boot-basics T2/T3 (by id, 404), spring-data-jpa T5 (record DTO + static from()), porting T2 (byId throws to @ExceptionHandler 404) and validation T2 (a class named ApiErrors, @RestControllerAdvice, forStatusAndDetail + setTitle('X not found')). Fine as spaced retrieval for a basic item, but if lab repos are allowed resources, the advice is a copy-paste from the learner's own lab (same class name and idiom). Fast-track learners skip labs, so the two tracks get unequal benefit.
findings.recommendation: Decide and publish the resource rule. If labs may be open, rename the advice class (e.g. ToolErrors) and require one detail the lab did not dictate (e.g. an extra 'toolId' property, which also covers the unobserved part of ProblemDetail#o1).

findings.claim: [all four items] Cueing across the same sitting: several final MCQ items show the code the coding items ask for. sfcp-q07 shows the exact advice code (forStatusAndDetail + setTitle) for Spring 10 and uses the phrase 'Refund exceeds the captured amount', close to Python 20's 409 detail. sfcp-q12 tests the same int-is-not-coerced-to-str fact as Python 10 check 4. sfcp-q39 shows response_model + Depends + HTTPException for Python 20. sfcp-q04 explains @Transactional self-invocation for Spring 20 (N9). If the MCQ comes first and stays viewable, the MCQ is a crib sheet.
findings.recommendation: Lock the MCQ (no review) before the coding items open, or put the coding items first. Optionally re-skin the q07 wording so it does not echo Python 20's detail text.

location.selector: originally spring-short-coding/spring-10min/README.md line 124 (not part of this item's landed files)

findings.claim: [all four items] The programme timing is stale and has no slack. Both Spring handoffs model the final day as 60+10+20+10+20 = 120 minutes 'zero slack', but the MCQ report moved the MCQ to 90 minutes (150 in total). Setup (go-offline 71-91 s per Spring repo, plus pip installs) is assumed to be pre-cached, and .evolv/grade.yml is unverified in Exa. If the template is not pre-cached, learners lose coding minutes or the timer start is ambiguous.
findings.recommendation: Update both handoffs to the current total. Require pre-cached Exa templates as a release gate (verify grade.yml in Exa). Add 5-10 minutes of buffer between items and state who starts each timer.

location.selector: originally spring-short-coding/spring-20min/README.md line 77 (not part of this item's landed files)

findings.claim: [all four items] No item has learner timing. All four time-boxes come from authoring estimates or agent cold-solves (Spring 7/15 min, Python 7/13 min median). For a final assessment where a timeout scores whatever checks passed, that is the main validity risk.
findings.recommendation: Run a timed pilot (3-5 Standard and 2-3 Fast learners, or TA proxies) on the target platform, and adjust caps or scope before release.

findings.claim: [all four items] The READMEs lack two sections that lab-contract.md section 1 requires: an 'Expected output' section pointing to expected/ (Spring only says 'prints nothing'; Python never mentions expected/) and an offline note. All four READMEs are also proven only on macOS arm64.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line Expected output section and an offline note to each README, and run once on Ubuntu and Windows (or the Exa template) before release.

findings.claim: [all four items] Learner-adjacent ids and docstrings say 'checkpoint' (spring-checkpoint-basic-tool-by-id; ToolLookupTest 'Spring checkpoint question I'), while the README says 'final assessment'. The same mix appears in Spring 20 (spring-checkpoint-intermediate-place-order).
findings.recommendation: Rename the ids and test docstrings to 'final' consistently across all four items, once the owner picks the term.
